dublinCore.title: Bilinear Transform and Frequency Warping
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Bilinear transform
Impulse invariance
Frequency warping
Prewarping
IIR filter design
Butterworth filter
Aliasing
dublinCore.description: Interactive MicroSim that converts an analog Butterworth low-pass filter to a digital filter with the bilinear transform s = (2/T)(z - 1)/(z + 1) and with impulse invariance z = e^(sT). A warping plot with a draggable analog-frequency marker compares omega = 2 arctan(Omega T/2) with the linear but aliasing omega = Omega T; an s-plane with a draggable test pole shows its images in the z-plane under both mappings; and overlaid magnitude responses with a gain table show the shifted cutoff without prewarping and the aliasing of impulse invariance near the Nyquist frequency.
relation: Chapter 10: Advanced Filter Design and Implementation

learningObjectives: Calculate the digital frequency omega = 2 arctan(Omega T/2) that the bilinear transform assigns to an analog frequency, and the prewarped analog cutoff Omega_c = (2/T) tan(omega_c/2) that places a digital cutoff exactly
Compare how the two methods map the j-Omega axis: a one-to-one compression onto the unit circle versus a linear map that wraps around the circle once every fs
Analyze the aliasing error of impulse invariance in the passband and at fs/2, and explain why the bilinear Butterworth response is exactly zero at fs/2
Predict where an s-plane pole lands in the z-plane under z = e^(sT) and z = (1 + sT/2)/(1 - sT/2), and verify that the left half-plane maps inside the unit circle
Evaluate when prewarping matters by measuring the bilinear -3 dB point at different ratios fc/fs
prerequisites: Poles in the s-plane and the z-plane

misconceptions.correction: Prewarping matches one frequency (the cutoff); the rest of the response is still compressed toward fs/2
misconceptions.evidence: With the defaults and prewarping on, the bilinear -3 dB point is exactly 2.00 kHz, but at 3.00 kHz the bilinear gain is -15.4 dB against -7.8 dB for the analog target

misconceptions.misconception: Impulse invariance is distortion-free because omega = Omega T is linear
misconceptions.correction: Each digital frequency also collects the analog response from fs - f, fs + f and so on, so the response is aliased
misconceptions.evidence: With the defaults the impulse-invariant gain at fs/2 is -6.6 dB instead of -12.3 dB, and with N = 1 the DC gain is +5.9 dB

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Four linked views of the bilinear transform and impulse invariance. A warping plot shows digital frequency omega against analog frequency: the bilinear curve omega = 2 arctan(Omega T / 2) and the straight line omega = Omega T of impulse invariance, which folds back above half the sampling rate. A gold marker on that plot can be dragged. An s-plane and a z-plane show a draggable test pole and its images under both mappings, and the poles of the filter. The bottom plot overlays the magnitude responses in dB of an analog Butterworth low-pass filter and its two digital versions, with a table of their gains. Sliders set the sampling rate, the cutoff and the filter order; checkboxes turn prewarping on and show the filter poles.

controls.label: Sampling rate fs
controls.description: Sets the sampling rate fs = 1/T; it moves the Nyquist line, the impulse-invariance strips and every digital design

controls.label: Cutoff fc
controls.description: Sets the desired cutoff of the Butterworth low-pass filter; its maximum follows 0.45 fs

controls.label: Butterworth order N
controls.description: Sets the order of the analog Butterworth prototype (1 to 4)

controls.label: Prewarp the cutoff
controls.description: Designs the bilinear prototype at fc' = (fs/pi) tan(pi fc/fs) so that the digital -3 dB point lands exactly on fc

controls.label: Show filter poles
controls.description: Shows the analog poles (gray, and blue when prewarped) in the s-plane and the bilinear (blue) and impulse-invariant (purple) poles and the bilinear zeros at z = -1 in the z-plane

visualElements.description: Warping plot: digital frequency omega (0 to pi, and in kHz) against analog frequency 0 to 8 kHz, with the bilinear curve, the impulse-invariance line folding above fs/2, the cutoff construction and a draggable gold marker
s-plane (s/2 pi in kHz) with the stable left half-plane, the j-Omega axis, the impulse-invariance strip edges at +-fs/2, the Butterworth poles and a draggable gold test pole
z-plane with the unit circle, the images of the test pole and of the j-Omega marker under both mappings, and the poles and zeros of both digital filters
Magnitude responses in dB of the analog target, the bilinear design and the impulse-invariant design from 0 to fs/2, with the aliasing gap shaded, -3 dB points and a hover read-out
Gain table (DC gain, -3 dB frequency, gain at fs/2) with plain-language notes on warping and aliasing; read-outs for the marker and the test pole

model.description: An analog Butterworth low-pass H_a(s) with poles wc e^{j pi (2k + N - 1)/(2N)} is converted to a digital filter by the bilinear transform (optionally with a prewarped prototype) and by impulse invariance via partial fractions; magnitude responses are evaluated on 361 frequencies from 0 to fs/2
equations: h[n] = T h_a(nT),  H(z) = sum_k T r_k / (1 - e^{s_k T} z^-1)
H(e^{j omega}) = sum_k H_a(j(omega - 2 pi k)/T)  (aliased sum, N >= 2)

instructionalStrategies: Predict the bilinear image of an analog frequency before dragging the marker
Compare the -3 dB point with and without prewarping
Drag a pole across the fs/2 line to see impulse invariance alias it
extensions: Add high-pass designs to show that impulse invariance fails for them
Plot the impulse responses of both digital filters against samples of h_a(t)
